Contract (problem.txt): out = sum_k a[k]*b[k] for float32 vectors, computed via split-K with atomic accumulation; bitwise agreement with any particular summation order is explicitly NOT required, only the mathematical inner product.

Source analysis: each program computes chunk = cdiv(K, SPLIT), start = part*chunk, and iterates off in [0, chunk) in BLOCK=256 strides with mask idx < min(start+chunk, K). Since SPLIT*chunk >= K and the per-partition ranges [start, start+chunk) are disjoint and consecutive, every index in [0,K) is visited exactly once and nothing beyond K is loaded (mask clamps to K); partitions whose start >= K contribute an exact 0.0 to the atomic. Out is freshly zeroed per call, so the atomic accumulation has a correct identity element.

Runtime evidence (tool event t6, claim c1): 18 lengths tested — 1, 2, 3, 7, 255, 256, 257, 511, 512, 513, 1000, 1023, 1024, 4096, 5000, 100000, 2^20, 2^20+37 — spanning K < SPLIT, K == SPLIT, exact multiples, and uneven tails. A ones-vs-ones coverage probe returned exactly K for every case (cov_err = 0.0 for all 18), which directly rules out skipped elements and double-counting, the classic split-K coverage bugs implied by cdiv partitioning. Against a float64 reference on randn inputs, max relative error was 4.21e-6 (K=1024, |ref|=2.96, abs_err=1.25e-5) and max absolute error 7.6e-4 at K=2^20 (|ref|=1024, rel 7.4e-7) — magnitudes consistent with fp32 per-partition accumulation plus atomic combination, i.e. the reordering the contract expressly allows, not a structural error.

Claim c1 was therefore rebutted, and no other contract requirement (dtype, output shape/dtype float32 length-1, partitioning as a free performance choice) is violated. Remaining untested cases (K=0, non-contiguous inputs, K large enough to overflow int32 index arithmetic) are not required by the stated contract and cannot support a reject.
